The Estonian law follows the same logic as German law. Courts in Germany commonly apply agency contract regulation to franchise agreements as well. h3. *§ 688.*  Right of agent to compensation for termination of contract and compensation for damage caused by termination of contract

 (1) An agent has the right to receive separate compensation (termination-of-contract compensation) upon termination of an agency contract if:

# the agent has created business relationships with new clients for a mandator or significantly extended the existing business relationships of the mandator, and
# the mandator has significantly benefited from such business relationships even after termination of the agency contract, and
# due to the termination of the agency contract, the agent loses the right to an agency fee which, had the contract continued, the agent would have been entitled to on contracts which were already entered into or would have been entered into in the future with persons who, as a result of the activities of the agent, entered into a permanent business relationship with the mandator for entry into contracts which were usually negotiated or entered into by the agent, and
# payment of compensation is justified taking into consideration all the circumstances.

 (2) An agent does not have the right to demand payment of a termination-of-contract compensation which exceeds the average annual fee of the five last years of the agent's activity or, if the agency contract was in force for a shorter period, a termination-of-contract compensation which exceeds the average annual fee of the entire period of the duration of the contract. If the agency contract was in force for less than one year, the agent does not have the right to demand payment of a compensation in an amount which exceeds the size of the agency fee earned during the entire term of the contract.

 (3) Payment of a termination-of-contract compensation does not preclude or restrict the right of an agent to demand compensation for damage caused to the agent by the termination of the agency contract. Such damage is presumed to exist if an agent does not receive the agency fee which the agent would have earned had the agency contract continued, while at the same time the mandator gained substantial income due to the activities of the agent. Such damage is also presumed to exist if the agent was unable to amortise expenses which the agent incurred due to performance of the agency contract and following the instructions provided by the mandator.

 (4) An agent does not have the right to a termination-of-contract compensation or compensation for damage specified in subsection (3) of this section if:

# the agency contract is cancelled by the agent, except in the case where the reason for cancellation is a circumstance dependent on the mandator or the age or state of health of the agent which does not enable the agent to continue the activities thereof;
# the agency contract is cancelled by the mandator due to the wrongful behaviour of the agent;
# after termination of a contract, the mandator and the agent enter into an agreement pursuant to which the agent is substituted by a third party who pays a fee to the departing agent in an amount equal to the termination-of-contract compensation and compensation for damage to which the agent would otherwise be entitled;
# acting as an agent was an ancillary activity of the agent.

 (5) Any agreements entered into before the termination of an agency contract which preclude or restrict the right of an agent to a termination-of-contract compensation or compensation for damage are void.

If we check the service code:

1 - The user lookup is using the phone number index. So there is not much to optimize there. This table is big once it stores all users,  even the inactive ones ({color:#ff5630}check after DB access{color}), and it is not sharded. Not on service, for sure, but even it it is sharded on DB level, the phone prefix would have to be stored in a separated column to work a sharding key.

2 - The user creation could be a problem, once it does not only create a user, but it also queries for a subscribe token and inserts an event on the same transaction. Also it retries for up to 10 times if collisions happens (most likely they don’t once they are uuids), but it again queries does other queries.

This part of the code starts here: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/3f8c0d63dd86f1487fbf4cd8fdafb83b05ca2384/src/platform/user/user/main/service/UserDataService.ts#L381|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/3f8c0d63dd86f1487fbf4cd8fdafb83b05ca2384/src/platform/user/user/main/service/UserDataService.ts#L381]

and this function really increases the chances of timeout: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/3f8c0d63dd86f1487fbf4cd8fdafb83b05ca2384/src/platform/user/user/main/service/UserDataService.ts#L680|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/3f8c0d63dd86f1487fbf4cd8fdafb83b05ca2384/src/platform/user/user/main/service/UserDataService.ts#L680]

3 - Last but not least, and event is sent and event data is inserted in the DB already outside the transaction, but as part of the service. It could be done in a FireAndForget, so it does not block the endpoint call for more time: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/3f8c0d63dd86f1487fbf4cd8fdafb83b05ca2384/src/platform/user/user/main/service/UserDataService.ts#L569|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/3f8c0d63dd86f1487fbf4cd8fdafb83b05ca2384/src/platform/user/user/main/service/UserDataService.ts#L569]

It looks like the amount of queries that run inside and outside the transactions and the amount of inserts and events are making this endpoint slow and probably the main cause of the timeouts.

*Exercises to be included:*

h3. *_Icebreaker/s:_*

*What makes them feel safe to speak up?*

Put team members into small groups and ask them to discuss in what circumstances they feel safe to speak up. If groups have difficulty getting started, you can prompt them by asking them to consider times when they haven’t felt comfortable speaking up. Elicit stories including where they were and what it was that made them uncomfortable. From here, encourage them to brainstorm factors that make it more likely for them to feel safe sharing their opinions and addressing potentially contentious topics.

Allow groups 5-10 minutes for their discussion. Then bring the group back together and table some answers or go right into presenting the concept of psychological safety to the group. Consult on psychological safety and why it’s important. Circulate the definition of psychological safety among the participants so that everyone understands the concept before going on to further activities.

h3. *Possible activities that can be used:*

*_Uncover the stinky fish:_*

The Stinky Fish Canvas is a quick way to uncover silent problems. It’s a metaphor for the issues that teams carry around, but which they either don’t want or don’t care to talk about.

The problem is that the longer we hide them, the stinkier our issues get.

*_The Stinky Fish Canvas helps teams identify four types of issues:_*

* What everybody is thinking but no one is saying (silent problems)
* The uncertainties that make people feel that they lost control (unknowns)
* Things that are making people feel nervous or lose their focus (anxieties)
* The emotions that get in the way and paralyze us (fear)

This exercise can be used to address overall team cultural tensions or during a particular transition (i.e. change of strategy, a new manager taking over the team, etc.) This ties in with recent changes within the CS department.

*_Session facilitation:_*

# Introduce the goal of the exercise. Set a safe space for people to be candid and speak up. Clarify that the intention is to uncover silent problems so that the team can solve them. It’s not a venting session, though.
# Display the image below on a Jamboard. This will allow each person to add their sticky notes under each question when prompted to do so. Some may be reluctant to share so I will start first (NOTE: the image would need to be added manually).
# As we go through the questions, note responses.
# Discuss commonalities, tensions, and contradictions. Prioritize the key issues that the team wants to address. Give each participant three votes (the issue that’s hurting us the most, the one that’s the easiest to fix, and the one that will help us the most).
# We can then move on to brainstorming solutions or table them and follow up.

Checklist for kafka optimisations:

* THP now opt-in /  always \[madvise] never - /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled ([https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/transparent-huge-pages/|https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/transparent-huge-pages/|smart-link] )
* tune filesystem [https://kafka.apache.org/documentation.html#ext4|https://kafka.apache.org/documentation.html#ext4|smart-link] 

* {{queued.max.requests}}: This sets the queue size that holds the pending messages while others are being processed by the IO threads. If the queue is full, the network threads will stop accepting any more messages. If you have erratic loads in your application, you need to set {{queued.max.requests}} to a value at which it will not throttle. Increased to 1000 from 500. Based on [https://community.cloudera.com/t5/Support-Questions/Any-tips-on-how-to-optimize-Kafka-broker-performance/m-p/169478|https://community.cloudera.com/t5/Support-Questions/Any-tips-on-how-to-optimize-Kafka-broker-performance/m-p/169478|smart-link]

In general, no statutory right exists for employees to be granted sabbaticals, no legislation specifically covers this area. This means that the only rules are those in employees' contracts or in a company policy. Despite the fact that sabbatical leave is an optional benefit meaning that the employer may set forth their own rules as they see fit, the employer still needs to take into account non-discrimination and unequal treatment rules. The terms of the sabbatical leave are provided by the employers and they are different across the companies. In most cases, sabbatical leave terms are based on the length of employment, considering how long an employee has worked for the company. Some organizations tend to follow the policy which provides that every employee, who has worked for 5 years at the company, is eligible to take a sabbatical leave. However, this raises questions, such as, what happens to employees, who work part-time or fixed term contract, or employees, who were “forced” to take leaves, such as parental leaves, or sick leaves during these 5 years - are those leaves included and considered as working time or not; and can we exclude such leaves from the calculation of working time.

From a legal perspective, this arises a question of discrimination and unequal treatment. It can be a complex matter because it may not always be directly regulated by laws, and it may vary in jurisdictions, however, some general principles apply. According to EU equal treatment and non-discrimination laws, when establishing working conditions and remuneration for the employees the employer cannot discriminate the employee based on protected characteristics: nationality (ethnic origin), sex, race, colour, religion or other beliefs, age, disability, or sexual orientation. Although it is debatable whether sabbatical or other employees’ benefits mean working conditions or remuneration, the equal treatment and non-discrimination regulation must be taken into consideration when establishing different types of employees’ benefit policies. It also needs mentioning that the employer is obliged to take the appropriate measures to protect employees against discrimination for promoting the principle of equal treatment.

Discrimination can be direct or indirect. +Direct discrimination+ is taken to occur where, on grounds of any protected characteristic specified in above, one person is treated less favorably than another in a comparable situation. For example, someone is not offered a promotion because they're a woman and the job is given to a less qualified man. +Indirect discrimination+ happens when an apparently neutral criteria applies for everyone but puts a person with protected characteristic in a disadvantage compared with other persons. For example, to apply for a job position everyone must take a physical fitness test which can put older people at a disadvantage. However, there is an exception when a situation is not considered as indirect discrimination. The differential treatment must be justified. The employer must show that the discriminatory action was both reasonable and necessary (in legal language: criteria is objectively justified by a legitimate aim and the means of achieving that aim are appropriate and necessary). In practice, it can be difficult to distinguish between indirect discrimination and permitted differential treatment.

 

*Parental leave, sick leave*

* As a short overview on other companies’ approach, according to common practice, parental leave is not considered active working time and therefore is not included in the “length of the working time” in sabbatical policies. While men are able to choose not to take parental leave, women are forced to take some time off from work when they are in labor (maternity leave). It is still up to the employer, whether they include part of parental leave as an active working time or not, however, there is a risk of violation of gender equality in the form of indirect discrimination like explained above as it puts women into disadvantages.

* As for the sick leave, most companies compensate part of sick leave and some have a policy, that gives an employee 3 extra days per year paid sick leave, which are considered as active work. Long-term sick leave is usually considered as time off from work and is not considered an active service of work. However, in this kind of approach there is a risk of violation of age or disability equality in the form of indirect discrimination like explained above as it puts older and/or disabled employees into disadvantages.

*Part-time and fixed term employees*

Under EU laws, the employer cannot treat employees working on part-time less favorably than the comparable full-time employees; And, the employer cannot treat with fixed term employment less favorably than comparable employees who have employment with unspecified term. Comparable employees are the same category employees, meaning that they have same or similar job duties, obligations, degree of responsibility, considering the employee's qualifications and professional skills. For example, all mechanics employed either for part time or full time are comparable and must be treated equally.

Thus, part-time and fixed term employees cannot be excluded from the sabbatical leave eligibility only due to the fact that their employment is either part-time or with a fixed term.  

 *Potential solution*

To mitigate the discrimination risk and violation of equal treatment when establishing the policy is to have a reasonable justification on differences of treatment that is based on objective grounds. Employer's policy or actions must be neutral, difference of treatment must be reasonable and necessary. Also, comparable employees must not be treated differently.

One of the approaches might be that employee irrespective of part time or full time/fixed term or indefinite term is eligible for the sabbatical leave in case of x amount of consecutive working time (active work) in the company which includes any types of leaves (non-active work) in total of x time. To be objective and neutral, Bolt wants to award such employees who have continuously contributed their effort to Bolt based on the length of their active working time. In such case we avoid pointing out a specific feature that may lead to discrimination and +reduce+ (not fully eliminating) indirect discrimination risk. Also, additional requirement for the eligibility could be that within the length of service, the employee has not been under disciplinary proceedings, e.g. they have satisfactory work record.

 Here are a couple of examples for the wording:

_" Employee eligible for the sabbatical is an employee who has been working consecutively at Bolt for 5 years within the last 6 years."_ Or "_Employee eligible for the sabbatical is an employee who has been working consecutively for 5 years. This includes absences from work for any reasons that do not exceed 6 months in total within the 5-year period.”_

 This version proposes that the employee has performed 5 years of active work, he/she might have taken any kind of leave, however, their active work still sums up as 5 years of service within the last 6 years. This version also proposes that an employee has worked hard for 5 active years within the last 6 years, and they deserve a sabbatical leave. Of course, the numbers in this example can be changed (note that UK law provides that any length of service criterion of five years or less applied in respect of an employee benefit is automatically permitted without the need for the employer to justify it). The logic behind this version is that it does not point out protected characteristics of employees which may lead to direct discrimination and reduces indirect discrimination, because we’ve considered length of the maternity leave.

Analysis:

There’s a baseline usage of about 30MB from the master process.
Each worker adds somewhere between 20 and 100MB (likely <50MB), per-worker.
Each instance of the model then adds 3.7GB.

With preloading and some GC micro-management, there’s one instance of the model per-server.
Without preloading, there’s N instances of the model for N workers.

The run-time performance of the server is not affected significantly by the number of workers (final result in most recent data is high due to other jobs starting on the machine).
The start-up time of the server is affected considerably by preloading (or lack of).  Preloading means we load the model only once (O(1)), while no-preload means we have to load the model in each worker (O(N), ignoring the block cache).

#  Using User ID in links is dangerous as it may be accessed by hackers or other external parties that is spoofing a network, if a breach happens they may be able to collect this information which they can use to escalate the breach by combining it with other intervals and gain more information about the end-user. # Input or output-encode all data coming into or out of the application to prevent unwanted code execution.
# Whitelist allowed URL values to still allow some execution but only from trusted sources.
# As backup and best practice, consider implementing Content Security Policy (CSP) for this host to protect against such injection type attacks.

You can review to see what works for this host. Likely depending on the technology used, there may be more granular solutions or best practice encoders, but these are the generic action items that can help mitigate the risk.

Hello Casper, 

Thank you for reporting. 

This driver is accepting rides and not going towards the pickup locations, then cancels the rides after marking as arrived - Aside from the ride triggering the rule “DRIVER_DID_NOT_PICK_UP_RIDER”, there are also 18 rides tagged as “RIDE_TOO_SHORT_TIME” within the past month.

We automatically block if they have many of such rides because:

* We preauthorise the ride price from the rider’s card to secure the payment and avoid failed payments/fraud, and when the ride is cancelled, sometimes it may take a day or two for the bank to release this money and this causes tickets to CS and overall inconvenience.
* The rider gets a notification that the driver accepted the ride, but then nothing happens, and we don’t automatically match them with a new driver when the ride is cancelled, so they need to go through the order steps again to place a new one, and in addition they might get a different price compared to the cancelled ride.

This can create a very bad user experience for our riders.

If the driver doesn’t want to do the ride, then they should reject it when they first receive the offer, and not right after they accept it.

I’ve removed the block as this driver has quite many rides and good ratings. It is also very good that the driver was educated about this and about contacting CS.

Best,

Francesca

Hi [~accountid:5ced0aef3b8abb0fc31a5112], let’s try the response below. I hope the lessor sees that it is reasonable and agrees to our calculation method.

_Hi Anna,_

_In both of the contracts for Tulika 15/17 dated 27.08.2021 and for Kaluri 3 dated 22.10.2021 we have a provision allowing the lessor to change the amount of rent in accordance with the changes in the CPI published by the Statistics Estonia. Such changes to the amount of rent will then be effective for a year until the next change, if any._

_In this regard, we do not see any reason why we could take the CPI increase for the separate month of June 2022 compared to June 2021 and use this number as a basis for increasing the rent for the whole future period of a year. Using the number from one month to increase the rent for a period of a year seems neither proportional nor reasonable._

_As Statistics Estonia publishes changes to CPI each month, it is our position that the rent increase should be based on the_ +_average of CPI increases for each of 12 months preceding the month of rent increase_+_. This means that we should take into account the CPI increase for each separate month of such 12 preceding months, add these numbers and divide them by 12. The reason for such calculation is that each month the CPI change could vary drastically, moreover it can both increase and decrease. Hence, to receive the balanced number, average CPI change should be used as a reference point for the rent change._

_Consequently, for the property at Tulika 15/17 the average CPI increase for 12 months from August 2021 to July 2022 should be calculated and used as a reference point for the rent increase, and for the property at Kaluri 3 - the average CPI increase for 12 months from November 2021 to October 2022._

_Please let us know if you agree with the above and we hope for your understanding._

I agree that the penalty is unproportionally high. Bolt is a global IT company with high values in keeping all data confidential. It is not reasonable even to introduce such high penalty, also in any event, the other party may always claim damages under the law so this - in my view - goes beyond the scope of an NDA and beyond. Perhaps financing conditions impact our pricing, whereas such decisions should be under discretion of Bolt and not dependent on a financing entity. Either this wording is too broad for clarity and should be specified or we should reason better with them why we may use some information to the benefit of Bolt.

By the way, I have been discussing the SOP/process for underaged rental riders for some time already with Alessandro and Liina. 

There is really no way to verify the user’s age. I asked the Legal team whether it is ok to verify the age with Veriff, and they told me smth about this being heavy on privacy because Veriff is meant for identity, not age verification. So what I understood from the replies there was that Veriff for age verification is a no go.

*Since we still receive reports about those underaged riders, I proposed the following process (even if only temporarily), Alessandro and Liina agreed:*

* _As we cannot use Veriff for age verification, let’s go with asking the user if they’re underage or not_

* _If they say they are, we keep their account blocked_
* _If they say they’re not, we remove the block. This is not ideal, but it is still better to document at least something. Otherwise, CS might still use Veriff for that because we have no other guidelines in place._

_If local teams have issues with it (e.g. underaged rental riders are a huge threat in their market), they can go to ID&T team with the data and request the in-app verification feature to be enabled (as it currently is in Modena, Bordeaux and Norway). If local teams insist on using Veriff (e.g. because the in-app verification cannot be implemented on their market), they can ask permission from the legal team. If they give a green light, we’ll add it to the process._

----

So, as we are just asking the users about their age when we receive such reports, I think we can also believe the users when they say they’re not underage and accidentally entered an incorrect DOB. This is also not ideal and there’s a chance that users may be lying, but we don’t have any other option honestly 🤷‍♀️ As Romain is only back next week, I propose we just let agents change the DOB of those users. If anyone has an issue, they can push for Product for a solution, but atm we don’t have it. Or if they want to use Veriff, the Legal team needs to give a green light for that. Once Romain is back, he can reply in the thread and let us know if there’s an alternative solution.

The current [process|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360013586780--User-requests-changing-account-details] mentions asking for selfie+ID or using Veriff. As both are a no-go (the process is outdated), I would suggest changing it to what I described above.

h3. *Metrics*

A score of 45 (9 questions carrying a weight of 5 points) per agent would represent the most psychologically safe team in the world. This is _somewhat_ unlikely. In reality, a score of 45 may highlight an issue where people feel unable to answer truthfully, so investigate further if that is the case.

The lower the aggregate score for the team, the lower the general psychological safety. However, the power of this survey is really in the *detail*.

Identify the statements with the *lowest scores and the widest range of responses*. These are your areas that require action and are where you can make the largest difference whether you’re in charge of the team or not. It may be, for example, that there are new team members who don’t feel as safe as the team members with a longer tenure.

Read the rationale for each statement below and This will help in considering what actions can be taken or behaviours can encourage raising the scores.

h3. *What do I do now?*

After using the survey, take some actions to address any issues that have arisen. If you ignore the results, you could inadvertently damage psychological safety and make it more difficult to address in the future. Where teams score low for any of the questions, take a look below and see what actions could be taken as a result.

h4. *1 – On this team, I understand what is expected of me.*

It is essential that team members understand what is expected of them in terms of delivery (speed, quality, cost, and other factors) and behaviour (everything from dress code and punctuality to coding standards) to foster psychological safety. Ensure tasks are clear and well defined, behaviour expectations are explicit, and negative behaviours are dealt with.

h4. *2 –  If I make a mistake on this team, it is never held against me.*

A psychologically safe team will never blame a member of the team for a genuine mistake if their intentions were good. Indeed, by enabling mistakes to be made without fear of blame, you enable innovation and risk-taking that can drive your organisation ahead of the competition. Utilise systems thinking and DevOps approaches to prevent mistakes before they happen or mitigate the impact of mistakes when they do.

h4. *3 – It is safe for me to take a risk on this team.*

Mistakes happen unintentionally, but risks are about taking actions that might not work or may have unintended consequences. Psychological safety provides the framework for positive risk-taking, enabling innovation and ultimately, competitive advantage.

h4. *4 – It is easy for me to ask other members of this team for help.*

In psychologically unsafe teams, team members try to hide their perceived weaknesses or vulnerabilities, which prevents them from asking for help. In a psychologically safe team, members prioritise the team goals over individual goals. Helping others helps achieve the team goal, and because team members feel safe to ask for that help, psychologically safe teams achieve more of their goals than unsafe teams.

h4. *5 – Members of this team never reject others for being different and nobody is left out.*

[+Evidence shows that diversity in a team results in higher quality products and happier team members+|https://hbr.org/2016/11/why-diverse-teams-are-smarter], but diversity in itself is not enough: it is crucial that team members are all included in decision-making and delivering results. To facilitate psychological safety (and high performance) every member of the team needs to be invested in the decisions made and the outcomes generated. This is particularly crucial for remote and distributed teams, where it is more difficult to see if a team member is becoming disengaged.

h4. *6 – Nobody on this team would deliberately act in a way that undermines my efforts.* 

In an unsafe team, members compete with each other to achieve their individual goals, and may even undermine other team members if it could benefit them or if it is perceived that doing so may elevate their “rank” within the team or organisation. In a psychologically safe team, that counter-productive competition doesn’t exist, and the success of the team is more important than looking good in the eyes of others.

h4. *7 – Working with members of this team, my unique skills and talents are valued and utilised.*

We all bring our own unique experiences, skills and knowledge to the teams that we’re in, but we also bring our own prejudices and biases. In a psychologically safe team where members are valued for being their true selves, biases are less likely to manifest. Indeed, team members may feel safe enough to identify, raise, and discuss their own biases or those of other team members. By doing so, we provide space for each individual to maximise their potential by utilising their own unique skills and talents.

h4. *8 – All members of this team feel able to bring up problems and tough issues.*

In a psychologically safe team, all members of the team are able to bring up problems and tough issues, ranging from personal struggles to concerns about other (even senior) members of the team. This psychological safety is crucial for allowing both _vulnerability_ to show when you’re struggling and need help, and _courage_ to raise difficult topics.

h4. *9 – My manager is able to resolve conflicts.*

 Managers are able to address issues or conflicts as soon as they occur and nip them in the bud. When arguments arise in the workplace, productivity typically declines. It can be difficult to focus or work together on a project when underlying conflict is present. Resolving these issues at the root can lead to greater efficiency and goal achievement.

Hey

Here are my general thoughts on the current setup - they are mostly connected to leaving an audit trail:

# My first thought is connected to the 3rd step of the 1st process – checking the data of the future driver. As far as I know, we are asking to present excerpt from the penal registry to check if the driver passes the threshold or not. As this is the first filter, maybe this would be good place to implement some additional checks – do we know what report can people take from the state? Does SRS issue some certificate that the person has no outstanding debts? I see no issue is the person has enforcement proceedings active – earning some revenue helps to alleviate that. But if they have active depts, that have not been contested – that might rise some red flags.
## As many companies are relying on the banking services and availability of banking services, they are implementing extra precautions and gathering information about their clients. Know Your Customer light-version could be a solution here (we are interested in possible risks that come with the persons – maybe the scope could be past companies they rendered service via).  This could be a simple step in the registration process and if asked, we can extract the data easily.
# My second thought is connected to changing the accounts and/or companies – 2nd process.
## We could ask the drivers who are moving from one company to another to confirm that as far as they know, all the outstanding obligations have been settled. Overall, if we could use something else than Google Forms, that would be good – any solution with AeS or QeS would be good.
## Changing the banking details – this is something that we should pay extra attention to. If the account changes from SEB to Swedbank – no problem. If it goes from SEB LV to SEB LT, but the names match – no issue. But if the driver’s name does not match the recipient’s name – should be investigated and additional information gathered. If the payment is done to high-risk areas – should be investigated and additional information gathered.
# Regarding the third process – it rises the administrative load, but I’d gather additional information about new fleet company – who is the CEO, who is the UBO. We could manually check if the new company has already known persons to us – then we should gather information, why they are changing the company (for an example: last company had taxi-service as minor activity; company was sold or bought, company split from the last one etc.). Generally, if one person (CEO or UBO) has a load of companies, it could indicate some level of risk (i.e., the companies are shells or dumped with obligations).
# Regarding the PoA-s: we should store them as long as the data protection rules allow. If necessary, make a copy of the physical PoA and store it.

Hey again,

Thank you for your reply and I agree that we could have some general guidelines in place.

 My understanding is that if the rider got from point A to point B, we technically don’t have to refund the trip. However, it might be that they were extremely dissatisfied/felt unsafe (e.g. the driver was falling asleep or made inappropriate comments), so we should issue compensation based on the severity of the issue and based how dissatisfied the user is. Bolt Balance makes more sense in such cases (because the trip was finished successfully) but then again the user might not want to use Bolt anymore, so BB is quite useless then. 

I wouldn’t say that there are cases in Safety where we 100% should not issue a full refund because of the reasons above (safety cases can be quite sensitive cases, even regular ones, and maybe sometimes BB refund might be seen as inappropriate so it is completely ok in my opinion to issue a full refund if the user is really mad). 

Also, just to mention: the Commerce team is working with our team on a task related to this which might change the compensation logic a bit and give CS the opportunity to revert a partial refund to a full one if needed (to avoid escalations to Commerce). Not sure how much Safety is affected, but just so you’d be aware since it is related to your request 🙂 

So to conclude: I’ll try to put together some comp guidelines and include them in the articles where we have none. Will be able to give you an update by EOD 🙂

Hi Sara, 

Based on the extract form her employment agreement, it seems that the candidate is subject to non-compete, meaning that she cannot work for a competitor (assuming Bolt is considered as a competitor of Wolt) for 12 months after termination of her employment with Wolt without Wolt’s prior consent. In case she joins Bolt without Wolt’s consent, she may violate her agreement with Wolt and Wolt may use legal remedies against her and against Bolt which may lead to costly and burdensome litigation.

However, please note that this is an initial assessment because I am not qualified on Georia’s laws, therefore I cannot comment the enforceability and scope of her non-compete agreement and what are exact legal consequences.  Also, the extract is quite vague on the restrictions, and I have my concerns about the enforceability and its scope. Could you please ask her is there any other agreements besides the extract she sent that regulate any post-employment restrictions, or any other relevant agreements which may affect her joining Bolt? We need to be aware of all agreements or other post-employment restrictions that may apply. Please remind the candidate that although post-employment restrictions are typically found in employment agreements, they can be found in other variety of docs (e.g. stand-alone non-compete agreement, additional compensation agreement). Please ask her also to send us her current job description.

Although Bolt is not directly responsible for her violation of her employment agreement, including post-employment restrictions, it still may largely affect us and there is a risk that Wolt would come also against us, even if turns out that post employment non-compete restrictions are not enforceable. Without going into details at this stage, risks involve violation of competitor’s commercial secrets/IP by the employee, i.e. disclosing such information to Bolt which may lead to IP infringement / violation of unfair competition rules by Bolt, etc.

Thus, if Bolt has solid desire to hire her and she’s genuinely interested of the position, then we need to fully analyse the implications and legal risks from Georgia’s law perspective to mitigate risks. Its also recommended for her to seek local legal advice to understand obligations and possibilities of joining Bolt.

As per the concerns related to fraud, whatever billing type/model/payment method they're on - after a ride is taken we always issue an invoice (no matter what) as a user/ride invoice. Now for resale, we issue a monthly invoice as well (such that business account don't have to use their individual ride invoices to reclaim VAT). For intermediate model we issue a statement (which can be used for accounting but they can't reclaim VAT). Furthermore, no matter if they're - resale/intermediate - the weekly PDF includes ALL rides taken within the month (but we don't check if the ride has been paid or not - the balance is visible on the BP). Now, they're a credit card based account meaning all rides got charged from the CC (we have the proof of payments available in Admin) so if they're claiming they can use it for fraud/money laundering etc. this should be taken to legal & they can confirm how it should work & then the team can prioritise fixing the logic.

Hey again\!

I’ve now specified some guidelines that hopefully help agents to make a decision on the compensation. Some articles that are describing more sensitive cases (and didn’t have comp guidelines in them) now have instructions to issue a full refund. *An example:* [Driver robbed or attempted to rob the rider|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4412540074770].

Other articles, where there can be more of this grey area, I’ve added instructions to take some things into account:

* Was the trip finished successfully (did the rider get to their destination)
* How upset the rider was (even if they got to their destination, were they feeling extremely unsafe/uncomfortable during the trip?) - this obviously depends on if and how the rider even expresses their feelings, but maybe it is helpful in some cases

*An example:* [Driver displays unprofessional behaviour|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4408893605394]

* _Based on the severity of the issue and the rider's experience, consider how much compensation to give to the rider_
** _For example, if the trip was finished successfully (and the rider got to their destination), it might not make sense to issue a full refund. Instead, consider refunding a small amount of the trip to the rider's Bolt Balance._
** _If the trip wasn't finished successfully/did not happen, issue a full refund to the original payment method_
** _If the trip was finished successfully but the rider is very upset (e.g. they mention feeling unsafe/uncomfortable during the whole trip), you can also consider issuing a full refund instead of adding money to Bolt Balance_

Also, specified that e.g. in cases where the vehicle was damaged, but the trip was finished successfully, it does not make sense to issue a full refund (but of course we still need to take it case by case, some people might feel unsafe in a damaged vehicle). *An example:* [Rider reports the vehicle was not fit for purpose|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4408910320914]

* _Based on the severity of the situation, consider issuing compensation to the rider_
** *_Note:_* _If the rider got to their destination, don't issue a full refund (unless it's a very edge case). Instead, issue a partial refund to their Bolt Balance._

----

PS. The changes in Beehive will be reflected in 1-2 hours. You can check the articles out and let me know if you have any comments/questions 🙂 I will close the ticket but as always, feel free to reply and I’ll reopen it.

Call with Hubert Kaźmierczak (Divisional People Partner Drive) on 19 August.

The purpose of the call was to identify any anomalies with previous Peakon results specific to CS. While he was not able to share the full data information with me, we discussed it over a call.

What was found is that there have been significantly small differences in the previous results. However, there were big jumps from 2021 to now. But there were drivers that did see low numbers and these are specific to:

# Future of Bolt
# Growth 
# Rewards

The first 2 points would need further looking into. This can be done during the workshops. Here, we can identify the main concerns of agents. This information can then be passed on to leads and devise a plan of action on how to address these. 

When it comes to rewards, this is a company-wide topic or concern and, while it can be discussed, it would take more time to solve and is highly dependent on top management. This means that there is not much we can change but we would need to wait for upcoming updates from the Comp. and Ben. team. 

What he did advise is that there seems to be a lack of awareness from CS agents about the People team, who is their dedicated People partner contact for the market, and what channels to use to get in touch with them (especially for cases of misconducted). He stated that there is a misunderstanding of what is considered ‘misconduct’ in the process. He also highlighted that each case is treated differently so there is no set rule on how, when, or if misconducted cases should be reported (unless it is gross misconduct that violates any employee or puts the company at risk or disrepute). What we can do is promote tools like SpeakUp to agents and they should not be afraid to report cases. 

Next would be to continue with the project/study. Once I have compiled the data and results, I can send him a report of my findings which can be utilized by his team.

Hey, Xoliswa\!

Thank you for raising these concerns. I do understand that this is not ideal, and that it’s difficult to handle questions from users when it seems that we’re not doing anything to help them. 

However, by taking the time to search for the charges and mark them as fraudulent as we were doing beforehand, we’re wasting both the user’s and CS agents' time because: 

# Marking payments as fraudulent (as we used to do for ride-hailing reports) doesn’t prevent any further fraudulent transactions from being made on the card on other platforms
# We were losing good GMV by blocking users & related devices (instead of blocking the card where the charges occurred, which is what we want to be able to do in future
# The time spent searching for charges is lengthy and adds significant cost to CS without creating value for the user or Bolt

The Fraud team have advised us it’s better for us just to wait for the bank to contact us or for a chargeback to come through. The best thing the user can do is block their bank card to prevent further charges. We realise this means there will be an increase in chargebacks, but that’s for the Fraud team to deal with.

This change is not the final solution, and the Fraud team assured me that they’re working on things from their side so that we’ll have a better process going forward. I’ll check in with them for an update to see if this will be done soon. If not, perhaps we can find an alternative for this process, so that our users feel that we’re actually helping.

Sorry that there’s not a better alternative at the moment\! I’ll get back to you as soon as I can 💐

[https://europe-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1088050327/1203227985|https://europe-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1088050327/1203227985]

[https://europe-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1087990118/1203154269|https://europe-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1087990118/1203154269]

[https://europe-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1087990010/1203153503|https://europe-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1087990010/1203153503]

We automatically block if they have many of such rides because:

* We preauthorise the ride price from the rider’s card to secure the payment and avoid failed payments/fraud, and when the ride is cancelled, sometimes it may take a day or two for the bank to release this money and this causes tickets to CS and overall inconvenience.
* The rider gets a notification that the driver accepted the ride, but then nothing happens, and we don’t automatically match them with a new driver when the ride is cancelled, so they need to go through the order steps again to place a new one, and in addition they might get a different price compared to the cancelled ride.

This can create a very bad user experience for our riders.

If the driver doesn’t want to do the ride, then they should reject it when they first receive the offer, and not right after they accept it.

I’ve removed the blocks as these drivers has quite many rides and good ratings. It is also very good and important that the drivers get educated about this and about contacting CS.

Best,

Francesca

Dear all,

Local entity employees signing contracts on behalf of Bolt Operations EE has been a BIG NO from a tax point of view and still is. We have clarified it more strongly in the signatory policy to avoid such practices.

If the contracts are concluded in a foreign country, Bolt Operations OU would be deemed to have a taxable presence in that country (permanent establishment) with related compliance requirements and requirement to pay taxes on B4B revenue in that country. Potentially this would also drag RH revenue to be taxable there through force of attraction principle. 

Consequently there is a contradiction where from one hand we tell the authorities that we currently run cross-border (centralized) business model whereas in practice we run the localized business (without relevant set-up).

If this is not viable for Ahto to sign all the contracts, have you considered Ahto giving a POA to a Bolt Operations OU employee located in Estonia to sign the agreements? We do also have B4B employees employed by HQ?

Erki.

Here is the case:

# Booking with small captured amount (e.g. 10 eur) is paid by a cash payment with bigger amount (e.g. 100 eur).
# Then several other bookings are also paid by this cash payment, but the cash payment are not completely spent on them and there is some remaining amount after that (e.g. 40 eur is spent and 60 eur remains).
# Then there is a cash adjustment for the first booking for -100 eur, which means that actually cash was not paid at all.
# The bookings from point 2 are “uncovered”, and the remaining negative amount goes to the first booking. 
# Then all that bookings from point 2 are covered again by remaining part of positive cash payment and remaining part of positive cash payment goes also to the first booking, but it is not enough to cover it.

After that all bookings are covered except the first booking which is “uncovered” for the amount of itself plus the amounts of bookings from point 2, which is bigger than the original amount of the first booking. More logically would be to “annihilate” these two +100 eur and -100 eur payments and leave all bookings uncovered for their original amounts.

Could you tell us if in Portugal there is any local policy (in the sense expressed above) that we should ensure our 3PLs comply with?

{color:#ff5630}*Note to Bolt:* {color}{color:#ff5630}_The recently enacted General Framework for the Prevention of Corruption (Decree-Law no. 109-E/2021) provides that entities with 50 or more employees must take measures to make their anticorruption policies and procedures (including code of conduct) known to third parties. As such, and considering that Clauses 2.1.e and 9.8.d already require compliance with Bolt Policies and Guidelines, we recommend that you discriminate_ {color}{color:#ff5630}*_any local anti-corruption instruments in the contract_*{color}{color:#ff5630} _or convey them in any other way to your 3PLs. For that purpose, we include a suggestion in comment in the attached agreement_{color}{color:#ff5630}.{color}

* *Warehouse ‘lease’ / Clause 4.* There are usually different scenarios possible for the warehouse:

i) the Contractor does not provide us with a warehouse (Bolt rents its own warehouse); or 

ii) the Contractor provides us with a warehouse (that he separately leases) for our exclusive use and in return we repay the full amount of the rent to the Contractor;

Regarding the second option, i.e. the Contractor provides us with a warehouse (that he separately  leases) for our exclusive use and in return we repay the full amount of the rent to the Contractor, our colleague from our HeadQuarters who specifically advises the Rentals business (and prepared the attached template for Estonia) provided the below advice: 

_The general rule should be that Bolt leases or sub-leases the warehouse directly and concludes a separate agreement for that purpose. The option of using 3pl’s warehouse as a service like it is regulated in the 4th clause and in clause 6 of Annex 1 should be used only in exceptional cases._
_From a legal perspective, the use of a warehouse is considered as a lease relationship. Although we have regulated in the agreement  that parties agree not to considers using 3pl’s warehouse as a lease relationship (see clause 4.10), in case of dispute it is worth noting that such arrangement may not be enforceable, and the court (depending on the jurisdictions) may deem it as a lease relationship. This means that Bolt could be considered as a lessee and the 3pl as a lessor, and obligations arising from a traditional  lease agreement (which are not regulated in our 3PL template) could cause disputes._

Could you please confirm whether clause 4 as currently drafted is sufficient and valid under Portuguese law for scenarios ii) mentioned above? If it’s not possible or too risky, could you please highlight what would be our options please? Would we have to enter into a separate lease?

{color:#ff5630}*Note to Bolt:*{color}{color:#ff5630} {color}{color:#ff5630}_These are bundled services provided  for a global fee (which includes all the services provided under the same – this is, for example, the Deployment, Collection, Battery swapping and warehouse services) and the use of the space of the Warehouse does not constitute the main scope of the Agreement. In this context, the regime established in clause 4 is commonly used for contracts whose services involve the use of facilities and, to the best of our knowledge, such fact has not been disputed in the courts. However, as already raised by Bolt, we cannot exclude the risk that a Court may consider this as a lease agreement. Notwithstanding all the previously mentioned, it should be highlighted that in case the Contractor is not the owner of the warehouse (being, therefore, the Contractor entitled by a lease agreement), use of the warehouse by Bolt is subject to the express authorisation of the owner of the warehouse. From a tax standpoint, the tax regime follows the legal/civil definition, whereas only pure leases – deployed of any additional services – are deemed VAT exempt._ {color}{color:#ff5630}*_Bundled service contracts do not qualify as a lease as such, and are subject to_* {color}{color:#ff5630}+*_23% VAT_*+{color}{color:#ff5630}*_._*{color}{color:#ff5630} _Having the above comments in consideration, we have inserted some suggestions regarding the different alternatives, notably not having a separate agreement for the warehouse services._  {color}

* *Insurance / Clause 2.1.n*

. Could you please advise on the local statutory regulation for employees in Portugal and the insurances that the contractor should have in place?

{color:#ff5630}*Note to Bolt*{color}{color:#ff5630}_: In relation to the employees, the contractor is required to cover them with an_ {color}{color:#ff5630}*_insurance against work accidents_*{color}{color:#ff5630}_. This insurance is mandatory according to Portuguese law and its terms and conditions mainly correspond to a standard policy legally approved._{color}

* *Mechanics*

Our Portuguese business team will also use some mechanics of the 3PL who will perform additional tasks. They want to reimburse the salary of these mechanics employed by the 3PL(“X” EUR per month per mechanic). 

We are aware that there may be employment lending risk in proceeding in this way. 

Indeed, our external counsel in Spain confirmed to us that, under Spanish law, any direct instruction from Bolt to the 3PL’s employees would be considered as an unlawful assignment of employees from the 3PL to Bolt. Therefore, they recommended including a provision whereby the 3PL appoints one of its employees as a “Service Coordinator” who receives instructions from Bolt and who communicates them to the rest of the 3PL’s employees. Bolt must not maintain direct contact with employees other than the Service Coordinator.

However, our external counsel in Belgium added some wording in clause 10 to set out the limited 'instructions' that Bolt can give to the 3PL’s employees. We copy this wording below in case this is helpful for Portugal and you think we should adopt the same. 

Our external counsel in Belgium confirmed to us that if Bolt does not exercise any employer's authority over the 3PL's employees and limits its instructions to those included in clause 10, chances of employees lending are basically non-existing.

{color:#ff5630}*Note to Bolt*{color}{color:#ff5630}_: The explanation of the legal risk and recommendation from a Spanish law perspective above also applies to the Portuguese jurisdiction. We usually recommend the same on similar cases –_ {color}{color:#ff5630}+*_Bolt should avoid to have direct contact with the contractor’s employees and all communications regarding the provision of the services shall be made to a Service Coordinator_*+ {color}{color:#ff5630}*_(who will then communicate any instructions to the remaining contractors’ employees)_*{color}{color:#ff5630}_. We have included a definition of “Service Coordinator” and adapted clause 10. of the contract for this purpose. We prefer this approach than the Belgium approach below, as Portuguese law does not detail which instructions could be given directly to the contractor’s employees and we prefer to_ {color}{color:#ff5630}*_avoid such direct communications at all, in order to reduce the employment risk involved_*{color}{color:#ff5630}_. In any case, our amendments to clause 10. of the contract include some of the principles mentioned below, clarifying which are the responsibilities of the contractor over its employees, making clear that Bolt does not have any authority over them.  Of course, this corresponds to what is written in the contract – which is important to mitigate the employment risk involved – but_ {color}{color:#ff5630}+*_the most important factor is the way the contract is executed on a daily basis (namely, if its execution complies with the principles defined on the contract)_*+{color}{color:#ff5630}_._{color}

Hi Romain,

thank you for providing Erik’s legal advice- this was very helpful.

As the verification is a regulatory requirement to verify user’s identity, the processing would be based on contractual necessity (article 6(1)(c) of GDPR) rather than consent, therefore no consent-like language would be required under data protection legislation.

As for the contractual provisions that would need to be in place:

(a) if the governmental database would be queried directly, the data transfer would occur between two independent data controllers, so strictly from regulatory perspective no data sharing agreement would be required. Of course if the authority would prefer to have some data protection arrangements in place, we can accommodate this request;

(b) if the verification would be carried out via 3rd party vendor then additional data processing agreement would be required to document the instructions and data protection measures that selected supplier should adhere to.

Finally, in order to address our transparency obligations, could you please confirm whether any details (apart from the driver’s license details) would be stored that would be acquired via BankID? If so, we would need to include that in our privacy policy.

Kind regards,

Adriana

You can find further information on how to set up our endpoint to collect original iOS 15+ SKAN postbacks here (it involves a quick change in the Xcode app settings by the app developers): https://support.appsflyer.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402320969617-Send-SKAN-postback-copies-directly-to-AppsFlyer-iOS-15-

We should be very cautious here not to publish misleading advertising. This is what UA laws say: 


Законом України «Про рекламу» передбачено, що недобросовісна реклама — це реклама, яка *вводить або може ввести в оману споживачів реклами*, завдати шкоди особам, державі чи суспільству внаслідок неточності, недостовірності, двозначності, перебільшення, замовчування, порушення вимог щодо часу, місця і способу розповсюдження.

If we continue with your ad, there’s a risk that users may think that the discount applies to everybody for every order, but it won’t. Users will be mislead and will report this to authorities and we can get in trouble. 

Thus, I recommend to use the following text in the ad: 
_Пропозиція дійсна при кожному замовлення від 300 грн та при деяких замовленнях на будь - яку суму._
_Щоб дізнатися, чи застосовується мінімальний ліміт 300 грн на Ваше замовлення, зайдіть у додаток Bolt. Ціни зі знижками будуть вказані на сторінці ресторану, і підсумкові ціни будуть видно при додаванні товарів у кошик._

Hey Team,

*Summary*
Not taken into account special possible cases, where the start- or end location would be sensitive (eg. Drug clinics, abortion centres,…) it seems that the disclosure of the first name (of the passenger (combined with the location data) during the time of the ride has a low risk (based on ENISA Methodology). 

{color:#ff991f}*A notification does not appear to be absolutely necessary, but could be argued (This will also depend on the fact, how often Links got activated (Amount of activated Links).*{color}

*But following steps are absolutely necessary:*
- Assess and document how the disclosure occurred despite prior determination that this data should not be included.
- Assess and report to the privacy team how often a link was activated.
- Development of measures to avoid/mitigate the risk of a similar incident in the future.

- [~accountid:5a9eaf7ca00c7f2a80156a09] mentioned that the “RiderTripSharing”-feature also includes the name of the Rider. I would recommend to check/evaluate if this information (Name Driver) in necessary and proportionate for the purpose.


*1.History*

Trip sharing is a feature that allows drivers to share a link with their real-time journey information. The link can be shared by Email, SMS, WhatsApp, Telegram, so that any third party with access to the link can follow the ride status and location in real time.

Links will remain active for up to 48 hours if a ride is not finished. Accessing a link after the ride is finished will notify the user that the link is expired.

The (open) link should not share information about riders. But we realized that we were sharing the Rider first name.

We released the feature on Aug 17, realized on Aug 18, and fixed (removing rider name) on Aug 22.

*2. Risk Evaluation (ENISA):* 

Based on the provided pdf-File we are talking about potential 261.352 cases ([~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e] is working on getting the number of cases, where the Link was activated by a third party)

Using the the ENISA Metrics the incident resulted into a Severity level:  *“low/medium risk”*:

*SE = DPC x EI + CBA* (Details at the EnD)
{color:#ff991f}*1,5* {color}= 2 x 0,5 + 0,5 

Even if the Severity Score leads to a “Low Risk” I would raise it to {color:#ff991f}*Low/Medium*{color} because of the amount of potential Cases

_(based on 3.3. of the ENISA Guidelines: Once the severity level has been defined, it can be accompanied by flags indicating certain elements of the breach that, although they do not affect a priori the scoring, they are important for the final assessment.)_

*4. Data Breach Notification*

In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority, unless the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons. 
--> The disclosure of the data contains a live view on the ride (during the ride) and a first name. 

Considering 
- The nature, sensitivity, and volume of personal data (per individual)
- Ease of identification of individuals
- Severity of consequences for individuals
- Special characteristics of the individual
- Special characteristics of the data controller
- The restricted amount of time the data was available (Links expire after the finished ride)
there is a low risk that the breach could result in *identity theft or fraud, physical harm, psychological distress, humiliation or damage to reputation.*
Nevertheless *the number of affected individuals* is high. 

{color:#ff991f}*The requirement of a notification therefore does not appear to be absolutely necessary, but would be be argued (This will also depend on the fact, how often Links got activated (Amount of activated Links)).*{color}


*4. Accountability and record keeping*
*4.1. Fixing the feature*

[~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e] stated that product-team fixed it. Also the created Links (unfinished rides) should be expired too.

*4.2. Evaluating (why did it happen)*
We have to assess and document how the disclosure occurred despite prior determination that this data should not be included (NOT as an internal blame game but to figure out how to mitigate the risk in the future)
[~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e] 

*4.3. Lessons learned and measures to mitigate risks in the future*
We have to develop measures to avoid/mitigate the risk of a similar incident in the future. [~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e] 

*5. More Details about the Risk evaluation*
*DPC (Data Processing context): 2*
The disclosure contains “simple data” (First name) combined with behavioural data (Location data). Using the ENISA methodology this with be valued with a score of *2*. _You could argue that The DPC score could be decreased by 1, because the nature of the data set does not provide any substantial insight to the individual’s behavioural information (“just” one ride), nevertheless the start/ending point could contain information about everyday life/habits (eg. Gym, Hospital,…)._ 

*Ease of identification (EI):* *0,5*
Identification can be direct or indirect and is performed with the use of certain identifiers, taking also into account the overall context of the processing of personal data. There are four levels of EI _(negligible (0,25), limited (0,50), significant (0,75), and maximum(1))_ with a linear increase in score. Because the link does not contain a full name, I would not consider the ease of identification as significant. Because of the fact that some first names could be rare, we can not assume that the it is _negligible → limited (_*_0,50_*_)_

*Circumstances of the breach (CB):* Based on Annex 3 of the “ENISA” recommendations: *0,5*

You could argue that the number of recipients are known. Nevertheless the Q&A mentions that anyone that receives the link from a driver can access it. There is the possibility to forward the mail to other parties

_Explanation:Based on Annex 3 of the “ENISA” recommendations_

_0 – Examples of data exposed to confidentiality risks without evidence that illegal processing has occurred. A paper file or laptop is lost during transit.  Equipment has been disposed without destruction of the personal data_

_+0.25 – Examples of data disposed to a number of known recipients_

_+0.5 – Examples of data disposed to an unknown number of recipients_

On the replacement of Jevgeni BELOUSSOV by Mahmoud Iskandarani as a managing director of BOLT SERVICES FRANCE SARL OC France indicated that there may be further employment law aspects that you may wish to consider as the incoming managing director (Mahmoud Iskandarani) is an employee of the company.

 

They have provided the following advice:

 

_" From a French employment law perspective, the combination of an employment contract and a corporate office can only be valid if meeting the following conditions (cumulative):_

_(a)_   *_Subordination_* _– There is a hierarchical relationship between the individual and the company in the framework of the employment contract and despite the corporate mandate_

_(b)_   *_Compensation_* _– The employment contract provides for a remuneration in consideration of the job duties_

_(c)_    *_Distinct technical duties_* _– In the framework of the employment relationship, the individual handles technical duties that are clearly distinct from the duties as corporate officer within the company._

 

_If failing to meet the above criteria, the combination of the employment contract and the corporate mandate will be deemed invalid: for as long as the corporate mandate will be effective, the employment contract will be on hold (suspension), depriving the individual from some employee-related benefits (such as healthcare/providence during employment and unemployment allowance after termination)._

 

_As a consequence, the main issue would be that in case of termination of the corporate mandate and the employment contract at the same time, the individual would not be eligible to unemployment benefits, failing to have validly contributed to the French unemployment agency (called “Pôle Emploi”). Besides, despite the above precautions, Pôle Emploi would not automatically grant allowances to the individual: it retains the capability to decide whether the combination was actually valid (and, therefore, whether the individual will be eligible to the unemployment allowances)._

 

_Given this uncertainty, companies can ask Pôle Emploi for their prior opinion in the framework of a specific process called “rescrit” and therefore have a clear position on the situation:_

* _In case Pôle Emploi confirms the validity of the combination, the individual will hold a guarantee he would be eligible to the unemployment allowances (subject to meeting all the other required conditions to qualify and to no modifications to his situation in the meantime);_
* _In case Pôle Emploi states the employment contract would not qualify, the company could decide to subscribe a voluntary unemployment cover for corporate officers (called “GSC”) to step in in lieu. Such cover is, in practice, paid by the company to the benefit of the individual._

_If not asking Pôle Emploi for their opinion, the company would knowingly take the risk the individual might not qualify to any unemployment cover, and could yet decide to mitigate it anyway by subscribing the above GSC."_

[~accountid:5c2db54163d3584fe075eb91] guided me to the code section within the {{react-commons}} where the {{session_id}} is defined.

* How are they generated/regenerated?
- They are generated on the eater app with the structure {{${userId | deviceId}eater${timestamp.now}}}
- {{session_id}}'s are generated whenever the eater has any interaction with the authentication flow ( login, logout, refresh a token, etc...).
- {{session_id}}'s are checked on every API request the app makes, if needed ( if the token has expired).
* What is the expiration time for a {{session_id}}?
- Currently it is configured in the {{eater-app}} to have a lifespan of 60 minutes.
* Can we make a {{session_id}} last for 90 minutes?
- From what I see yes, it's just a matter of updating the configuration of the app -> *this means that only future app versions will have the extended* {{session_id}} *lifespan.*

h1. *Summary of the STLs Interviews*:

_The Interviews were anonymous, which is why I will not be presenting any names or markets specifically. The narrative below is a representation of all the LoBs and the majority of our markets._

*_Pain Points:_*

* *The Contract.* It seems that OS Suppliers have a somewhat better understanding of what the contract constitutes than our STLs do and it is very often a shield for each OS Company to guard themselves against any feedback from the STLs. As long as the contractual KPIs are met, OS Suppliers will not go the extra mile and only act if the KPIs aren’t met again. This often creates problems, as our STLs strive for the best possible performance, regardless of the KPIs.
* *Wrong Expectations*. What came up often is the expectations set in the very beginning with the Suppliers by us as BOLT. In some markets, Suppliers do not treat STLs as people that can demand certain things and it looks like the hierarchy has never been addressed. A lot of STLs suggested that we should make the hierarchy and exact expectations very clear in the beginning because from their perspective they are expected to deliver nearly impossible things, taking into account that Suppliers have their contractual KPIs and do not respect STLs' position enough.
* *Huge Differences between OS Suppliers*. It seems that Majorel is the most stable OS Company and the most professional. Even though in certain markets they haven’t been easy to work with, it usually came down to the people that were hired. After proper feedback, it was usually addressed, even with a full replacement of personnel, which usually resulted in the visible improvement of collaboration. Other Companies, however, are way less stable. Surgo and Transcom have presented themselves as problematic but for different reasons. Surgo’s problem is often people - they are usually not selected well enough (speaking about the Agents, mainly) and the leadership struggles with taking any feedback from our side, turning very defensive. Unlike with Majorel, any discussions on the topic of poor quality of their workers, is met with defensive approach. With Transcom, the problem is that they do not want to do all that is needed to meet the KPIs. 
* *What Does it Mean to Keep them Accountable?* This was a surprisingly common point raised by the STLs - they have struggled with understanding what exactly is expected of them in this regard. If it is only to make sure the contractual KPIs are being met or that the entire market is healthy and the quality of replies is human? If it’s the former, it hasn’t been clearly communicated, as we usually are expected to deliver better results than the required minimum. However, if it’s the latter - then the potential problems lie in the contract and the way we set expectations for the Suppliers.
* *Non-unified Processes* - this point is my observation. While some STLs do own the Supplier Engagement, some simply leave it for their TLs. Interestingly enough, TLs do not always feel this is a bad idea - for some of them, it’s easier to directly address problems with Suppliers on their markets, rather than keep reporting those issues to the STLs. Some STLs, though, are regularly getting in touch with Suppiers through Silent WBRs, MBRs and through Escalation Sheets. On some markets STLs take more Admin duties, while TLs are handling day-to-day cases, on others - STLs are doing both.
* *Walking in the Dark* - nearly all of the STLs have raised the same point - they have been expected to deliver something, without any preparation from anyone. Most of them have been building the process through trial-and-error, they said some sort of a unified dashboard for tracking escalations could be very useful, or a unified space with the key knowledge elements on the crucial topics on How to Keep Suppliers Accountable.
* *Quality is Poor* - even if the contractual KPIs are met, all STLs have been consistently struggling with overall reply quality of the OS Agents. In some markets, there were even problems with a proper use of language - this is specific to Surgo, whose language entry exams for new hires are weird and not sufficient to determine the professionalism of the soon-to-be Agents. Regardless of the language, though, the quality has been a very often problem - CSAT does not always show if the reply is the one we have always strived for at BOLT - human. But, as presented in the points above, the contractual KPIs is what matter to the OS Partners. It seems that some STLs were able to push for better quality than others but it boiled down to the relationship between the parties.
* *Avoiding Responsibility -* Some OS Partners use the contract rule that allows to waive the contractual KPIs, whenever there were more tickets than predicted. If the prediction says 10,000 tickets but OS Company sees that it was 11,000, they can waive the FRT, for instance, as it would be impossible to achieve, and STLs have no grounds to expect improvement or narrative. While in theory it seems like a very good idea, in practice some STLs fear it is overused by the OS Suppliers but it is also very hard to prove.

*_Suggested Solutions:_*

* *Quality Team’s Vision* - I think that if [~accountid:5e2af04c895d5b0c97051eaf]'s vision will come true and Quality Framework will be implemented both among all Suppliers and in the contract, the issue will starting to be solved with each month. If there will be a framework that will make all Suppliers follow much more than just CSAT for contractual Quality KPI, then this should immediately help STLs to enforce or expect specific changes in the OS Companies' replies.
* *More Clarity on the Expectations and Hierarchy from the Supplier Engagement Team* - it looks like the entire thing cannot be improved without SET becoming more transparent with what exact expectations are presented to all Suppliers from the beginning. At the same time, it would be good if they could lay some groundwork or guidelines on what to do in case an OS person is behaving very poorly and affecting STLs work.
* *“Holding Suppliers Accountable”* *Course* - while initially, I didn’t think this would be needed, I’m starting to see the value after completing the Interviews with the STLs. They have mentioned that due to the changes in the CS, holding suppliers accountable will actually be one of the main responsibilities and that they really need to be supported more. The topics I believe would be good to implement there (some of them were my ideas, some of them were directly requested by the STLs):
** *_Negotiation_* _-_ how to present the goal to OS Partners and be able to achieve more by showing it’s the same. Ideally, live sessions with workshops and role play.
** *_Contract_* - more detailed explanation of what the contracts constitute. What are the potential loopholes and what are the exact agreements. If it’s different among Suppliers, it also should. be stressed.
** *_Internal Workflow in Case of Problems_* _-_ clear communication path, with names and teams to reach out to in case of any problems. If the SET would lay the groundwork and guidelines, we could use them in this Who is accountable for what and to what extent can Supplier Engagement Team help the CS Delivery.
** *_Suppliers Information_* - explaining the inherent differences between us and any Supplier. What many TLs and STLs struggle to understand, is this awareness that for Suppliers the context of a “client” and “feedback” is completely different than for us. Since they are experienced in working with companies like Microsoft, which is very inhumane in treating them as Outsourcers, they often treat our “feedback” as the extension of that attitude. They do not see it as we do - given with the intention of making sure we do our best.
** *_Supplier Differences_* - Each Company is slightly different, culturally, size-wise, etc. I think it would help to give this context to the STLs.
** *_Dashboards and Escalation Sheets_* - some suggestions on how to create useful and efficient Escalation Sheets between IN and OS Teams. What level of action steps do we expect from the OS Partners and how can we monitor they are completed. Again, SET perspective will be very valuable here.
