Hi,

even though (a) the agreement will be signed only for the trail period; and (b) the processing activities will be limited to the data acquisition; under GDPR this would be still considered engaging a processor and therefore require data processing agreement. As mentioned on Slack unfortunately we don’t have Spanish version of the DPA on hand.

As for the document itself - please see the responses below, I also included edits discussed in the doc attached:

*(1) Is the intention that the DPA is completed with Bolt as the data controller and the third party as the data processor? Or something else?*

The document is usually completed by the local team at Bolt who usually has the most extensive knowledge about planned partnership.

*(2) In relation to Annex 1, what are the relevant categories of personal data to fill in (paras. 3, 4 and 5)? The template doesn’t provide examples, but presumably there are fixed categories to apply? Any examples you do have would be handy.*

* Ad para 3 -  requires to specify who are the individuals whose data is in scope. In this case, this should be: Prospect Drivers, Drivers.
* Ad para 4 - categories of personal data acquired by the supplier should be listed there. There isn’t an exhaustive list of personal data that may be in scope (as the definition of personal data is very broad and it includes all information that may lead to direct or indirect identification of the data Subjects ), however given the plan set out here: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zL_bYgMmuOs2fQ_3i8ku9osHEzoTcAhYw_wrb8R5CTM/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zL_bYgMmuOs2fQ_3i8ku9osHEzoTcAhYw_wrb8R5CTM/edit|smart-link]  , I understand that scope would most probably include the following: first name, last name, date of birth, information included in the driver’s licence, photo of the data subject, information about the vehicle, phone number, e-mail address, insurance information, bank account details. The business owner of this process would most likely be able to confirm the final scope of data collected by the supplier.
* Ad para 5 - under GDPR special categories of data include: data revealing racial or ethnic origin political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data and biometric data processed for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health, data concerning a natural person’s sex life or sexual orientation. So in this scenario this should be: Not applicable.

*(3) For the purposes of Annex 2, which of the options is appropriate? It’s not obvious to me from reading the document.*

Option 1 as this is processing instructed directly by the controller (I made relevant changes to the doc.

*(4) After Annex 2, at the very end of the document there are four additional annexes (restarting with Annex 1). Do those annexes need renaming?*

I’d suggest not implement additional changes into Standard Contractual Clauses- this is set wording that has been approved by the European Commission and we cannot really make any changes to it, except where it is specifically required. However this is good point- we will make some changes and clean up our template in the following days for future use.

(5) The sections headed “*ANNEX II - Description of the processing*” and “*ANNEX III - Technical and organisational measures including technical and organisational measures to ensure the security of the data*” seem quite substantial to complete and I think it will just confuse the local team in its current form - they will not know the extent that detail is required. Presumably we have DPAs in place for other activation partners, in which case are there any available to hand (as examples)?

Re Annex II - I’d suggest to include information in line with the Annex 1 of the DPA. I filled it in - please note that the scope of data still needs to confirmed.

Re Annex III - I suggest to refer to our standard security requirements set out there.



BR,

Adriana

_Lugupeetud Marek Aunver_

_Kindlustustegevuse seadus § 219 lg 1 p 1 annab aluse õiguse isikuandmeid nõuda, kui need on vajalikud kindlustuslepingu täitmiseks, selle tagamiseks või tagasinõude esitamiseks. Bolt peab isikuandmete töötlemisel lähtuma sellest, et isikuandmeid töödeldaks vastavalt kehtivale regulatsioonile ja mistahes andmete väljastamine oleks seaduslik ja täidaks eesmärki. Meie hinnagul ei ole üksnes sündmuse lühikirjeldus piisav, et õigustada isikuandmete väljastamist küsitud koosseisus._

_Nõnda laia andmekoosseisu avaldamine peab olema põhistatud ja täitma eesmärki - peame oma tegevuses, sealhulgas andmete väljastamisel, järgmima minimaalsuse põhimõtet._

_Käesoleval juhul ei ole meil piisavalt informatsiooni, et isikuandmeid väljastada - kui isikuandmete teabenõue on konkreetne, see on faktiliselt ja õiguslikult põhistatud ning muud moodust andmete saamiseks ei ole, siis oleme valmis andmeid väljastama._

_Isikuandmeid väljastame nõnda nagu nad on süsteemi salvestatud - see tähendab, et saame korrektse päringu peale väljastada andmeid, mille väljastamine on põhistatud. Mistahes selgitused või hinnangud ei ole isikuandmete koosseisu osa ning nendele ei saa vastata isikuandmete päringu raames._

Tips paid in cash are not taxable. 

But that is the obligation of fleets and couriers, so I do not see any risks for Bolt.

Hi ladies, hope you are both well 🌻 

After reviewing the information you’ve provided in more detail, I have some updates and questions for you:

# Why don’t we share the specific reason for the document rejection in the email we send to drivers?
## According to the info [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iRZ-i2hJe3xjWU2PuB4CMPhngUAMwiHQEgI7GgUFFgE/edit#bookmark=id.nssco6uxe3g2], we only inform them which document was declined. We’re making life more difficult for the driver by asking them to click through to a self-help article, when we could present them with all of the necessary info right away. The more clicks a person has to do to find the info, the more friction we add and are just increasing the likelihood of driver churn.
## I think [~accountid:60630d4b8a0f7c006fb3738d] mentioned something about drivers not reading their emails? Please correct me if I’m wrong. However, if this is the case then we cannot expect that drivers will read through multiple FAQs to find the answers they need.
# The information about what is an acceptable/not acceptable document is covered in the [London document requirements|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CyhFsnzQ64C0spmbbp_rXv1w6r02VbK9mMwvDFFseak/edit#bookmark=id.nqnhhoeowwi2] article. Drivers will not scroll through articles in hope of finding the reason that their document was declined. For example, if a driver uploaded documents but were missing a supporting document, they would have to scan through multiple possible reasons as to why it could have been declined, and figure out which one applies to them.
# Overall, I found all of the information in the articles to be overwhelming, and I suspect that drivers would feel the same. As a driver, I just need to know why my document was declined on this specific occasion, I don’t need to know all of the possible reasons it may be declined
## Based on points 1 - 3, having a separate article for UK drivers about why their document has been declined does not make sense. We should just communicate this to drivers directly with the specific reason for their case.
# I’ve confirmed with the Product team that we cannot link different articles as “it provides a bad user experience”. Additionally, it can actually dilute the user’s focus and lead to them missing important information. We had previously hoped for a “related articles” section to be implemented, but this is currently not a priority on the Product team’s side.
## Due to this, having so many different articles for UK driver documents is not going to help driver churn because it just makes it even harder to find relevant information in the self-help space.
# Feedback for future requests: It’s much easier for us if you describe the problem statement, what info you believe to be missing, and the main struggles, rather than presenting pre-made articles. It is our team’s role to create and maintain information for the self-help and KB spaces and decide on the final layout and wording.

h2. Self-help content

These are the self-help articles related to accidents and accident-related fines:

* [https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360020653220-I-was-involved-in-an-accident|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360020653220-I-was-involved-in-an-accident|smart-link] 
* [https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4403097459602-Why-was-I-charged-a-fine-for-Bolt-Drive-|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4403097459602-Why-was-I-charged-a-fine-for-Bolt-Drive-|smart-link] 

We have to keep in mind, however, that self-help would not be a solution for:

* preventing this issue in the first place (users letting a third party drive a car they reserved)
* raising awareness +prior+ to any accidents (about insurance not applying for accidents by a third party driving the vehicle)

*Here’s what self-help content we can create about the insurance:*

* [https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4403097459602-Why-was-I-charged-a-fine-for-Bolt-Drive-|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4403097459602-Why-was-I-charged-a-fine-for-Bolt-Drive-|smart-link] - add details about insurance not applying if a third party was driving the Drive vehicle. This article would be checked by users who already got into an accident and received a fine to cover the damages in full.
* Create a new article _How does the Bolt Drive vehicle insurance work?_ - we could focus on the insurance details in a completely separate article. It could help raise awareness of existing users.

h2. Other resources (outside of our scope)

These are the resource where we already have details covering how the insurance works in case of accidents by a third party driving the Drive vehicle - and how we may or may not utilise them to raise awareness of the insurance part:

* [Drive T&C|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/ee/terms-for-bolt-drive/] and [List of Penalties and Additional Fees|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/5GkRPkxmEcRN1hUvkNAJm3/0d335f9d82763811365b59e93632733e/EE-EN_Bolt_Drive_Fines_Rev02.pdf] - these are legal docs that users agree with, and the insurance details are covered there. The issue, however, is that the majority of users probably don’t read these documents in full. The information is there but the issue is the lack of awareness of it.
* [Drive landing page|https://bolt.eu/en/drive/] - we mention accident-related fees and fines, as well as insurance. However, we don’t specify that the insurance doesn't apply to accident-related vehicle damages if the vehicle is driven by a third party. *The online Presence team could review if we should update the content accordingly (probably the FAQ section).*
* Verification flow - for new users, the verification flow is probably the best place to raise awareness of everything a user needs to know about verification and that only they can use the reserved vehicle. Perhaps _after the verification process is completed_ (after the address is entered) is a good place to show one or two stories with information about not letting third parties drive the reserved car, and what happens if they do that. 



[~accountid:623d6f0eee1b5a007029efb6] I’d appreciate your thoughts on:
- Whether the self-help content updates I suggest make sense
- Adding the informative stories at the end of the verification flow in the app (as a way to raise awareness of how the insurance works)
It’s not clear how to support it without building sth too generic.

_Customer not meeting a target provided in Annex 1 clause 2 for three consecutive months in a territory following six months from the first made ride in the territory shall be considered a material breach of the Agreement._

Last but not least, the above also plays into the 12 month initial period logic per c 6.5. _Having an initial term refers that for this period parties will be more relaxed - what Nick suggests cracks this logic to some extent._

So, currently how it works with Subscriptions:

# First payment: authorise, and then capture.
# Second and all subsequent payments: only capture.

For the first payment it works fine: we can say that we don’t want to use balance and if authorisation fails, then booking is cancelled and purchase is also cancelled.
For all other payments there is only “capture” which for us basically means that order has already happened and we need to take money for it, we cannot cancel it at this stage, so, we need to do our best to take the money, and that’s why we take money from balance if payment fails. This is the problem.But we can do it other way:

# First payment: authorise, and then capture.
# Second and all subsequent payments: also first authorise (but with {{user_present=false}}) and then capture.

But in this case we need to make sure that for the second and all subsequent payments there will be no 3DS checks or something else which requires user interaction. And if we do so, we can cancel booking and cancel subscription when its next payment fails. This way will also require development from Subscription side. But this is more correct way as I think.

Confirmed with Andrus that 3DS or user interaction will not happen in recurring subscription payment.

Update - apologies I forgot to add the preliminary advice received from external counsel (DLA) on 16 August - please see below and attached:

[^Bolt Mail - RE_ PT - RH - Pick-up point at Lisbon airport - [Private & Confidential] [DLAPIPERABBC-PRINCIPAL.FID933377].pdf]

+DLA preliminary assessment as regards the question about the reformulation of the areas of Lisbon Airport currently designated for both Taxis and Ride-hailing services+:

First, in accordance with the provisions of clause 5 of the concession contract, the object of the aforementioned concession is to provide Airport Activities and Services which include the "organisation of airport spaces, as well as the discipline of their occupation and use", the "circulation of Staff, Passengers and other Users as well as their modal transfer between all means of transport available at the airports", the "provision of publicly accessible car parks" and also "any other activities and services deemed necessary for the safe and efficient operation of airport infrastructures".

Second, the Concession Areas defined in Annex 2 to the contract +do include+ the parking areas of Lisbon Airport as well as the areas designated for the "pick up" of passengers by vehicles.

Furthermore, the concession agreement does +not+ contain any rule directly prohibiting the relocation of the areas currently designated as pick-up points (even though it may be considered to be a public service, as conveyed by ANA). Therefore, one of the first conclusions we may reach is that the wording of the concession contract does +not+ prevent ANA from deciding to relocate the places where ride-hailing drivers (together or separately with other users \[not including taxis]) pick up their passengers.

Other provisions of the concession agreement, together with provisions enshrined in the law supporting the concession, indicate that “the concessionaire has the powers and prerogatives of the grantor regarding: a) the licensing of the occupation and exercise of activities and services in assets of the public airport domain included within the scope of the concession, as well as regarding the practice of all acts relating to the execution, modification and cancellation of licenses and g) the preparation and application of regulatory standards within the scope of the concession activity, particularly in matters of security, environment and access and use of services included in the airport activities and services".

The legal set of powers resulting from all these provisions do, in our opinion, provide ANA with sufficient powers to take decisions in respect of the location of taxi passenger pick-up points.

Having said this, we must emphasize that under the terms of the general law, i.e. the regime provided for in article 16 of Decree-Law no. 251/98 of 11 August, it is the City Council's competence to establish by regulation the systems for parking taxis and to decide between free, conditioned, fixed or stopover systems. It is therefore the competence of the City Council to define the spots on the public road intended to be "taxi ranks".  

To conclude that ANA may indeed change the location of taxi passenger pick-up points at the airport one would have to assume that the concession framework creates a special rule vis-à-vis the general regime. We do think that the set of rules in place allows for this assumption and the resulting conclusion. However, we also consider that it is relevant to assess how the City Council and ANA themselves have interpreted and applied the law in the past in order to better understand the odds in case Bolt decides to challenge the understanding by ANA. If ANA has indeed followed one consistent interpretation and application of the law over time, the chances of challenging it are lower than if we detect inconsistencies.

In order to ascertain how exactly the City Council and ANA have interpreted the legal regime underlying the concession, we would have to ask the City Council for information in this respect. We should expect 10-15 working days in order to obtain a reply.

In light of the above:

#  our opinion is that *the legal set of powers resulting from all these provisions do provide ANA with sufficient powers to take decisions in respect of the location of taxi passenger pick-up points* and we are therefore in a position to move towards drafting the legal memo;
# *however, we cannot ignore the fact that the general legal regime attributes to the City Council the competence for the definition of taxi passenger pick-up points and that in order for this competence to be overridden, one has to assume that the concession regime has created a special rule in this respect. This assumption is not clear in the concession regime*;
# *the most effective way to clarify the doubts concerning the relationship between the general legal regime and the special concession regime would be to investigate how the City Council (and possibly ANA) have interpreted and applied the law in practice, for which an additional 10-15 working days would be required*.

+Considering the above, please advise as to whether:+

* you wish us to move immediately to the drafting of the legal memo, which will be drafted essentially on the basis of our own interpretation of the law and the applicable theoretical considerations;
* you prefer to have us consulting the City Council (on a no-name basis) and ask for information allowing to better understand what their interpretation and application of the law has been in the past, for which you should count an additional 10-15 working days.

Thanks

Usually random symmetric key, and IV, is generated by code used to encrypt the blob of data when the encryption process is started and key discarded as soon as it is not required anymore (encrypt it with private key). You then need to keep the IV (and authentication TAG \[AES-GCM]) and pass it with encrypted blob, but these can be plaintext.

Long story short - I would say no to keeping AES key and IV in secrets as they need to be unique for each encryption “round“, RSA keys are OK to store.

One example I could quickly find for AES +RSA can be found from here [https://github.com/java-crypto/cross_platform_crypto/blob/main/RsaAesGcmHybridEncryptionString/RsaAesGcmHybridEncryptionNodeJsCrypto.js|https://github.com/java-crypto/cross_platform_crypto/blob/main/RsaAesGcmHybridEncryptionString/RsaAesGcmHybridEncryptionNodeJsCrypto.js|smart-link]

Hi [~accountid:623c99a4d32a94006a64edf8] - I’m looking after this ticket in Shiv’s absense today.

I have reviewed the new licence and I'm comfortable that Bolt can proceed with entering into another arrangement with Regus on these terms. 

As you will know (and as Shiv has pointed out), there are various risks that are associated with an occupational licence, most notably a lack of security of occupation (i.e. it can end quickly) and the terms and conditions typically heavily favour the licensor (Regus). We are able to take a commercial view on the basis that the extent of Bolt’s exposure for licence fees is relatively nominal. Of course, this always needs considering on a case-by-case basis in the usual way so please continue to raise tickets for each licence for a sense check.

*Key points (cc.* [~accountid:60bd1b9a20d2dd0070e37ba0] and [~accountid:629736189bc7150068ce0c0e])*:*

(1) Proceeding on the basis of a month-to-month arrangement is acceptable and there is no commercial rationale for a licensor to terminate the arrangement so long as they are getting paid, although it does mean that the arrangement can theoretically end at short notice. A lack of security of occupation goes hand-in-hand with a cheap licence like this (the middle ground being a longer fixed term with adequate break options, and at the far end of the spectrum being a more expensive, longer term lease).

(2) Regus do have the ability to move Bolt to other nearby buildings if the office becomes unavailable for some reason (i.e. Regus themselves cease to have ownership of the building). This has caused us issues before. Regus have been previously unwilling to amend this provision but we are able to take a view on the basis that these circumstances should be unlikely and if we are moved, we can terminate on a month’s notice. Again, a lack of security of occupation goes hand-in-hand with a cheap licence like this (the alternative at the other end of the spectrum being a more expensive, longer term lease).

(3) I assume this is intended to be an ‘unmanned office’ in practice (as is often the case) but if that is not correct then do let me know. You should nevertheless familiarise yourself with the ‘house rules’ to ensure they are complied with.

(4) Before this licence is signed, please ensure that our regulatory team is satisfied that this meets their specific requirements and that all relevant information needed by that team is to hand ([~accountid:629736189bc7150068ce0c0e] / [~accountid:60bd1b9a20d2dd0070e37ba0]).

(5) I’m happy that this licence does not require director level signature but for oversight purposes it should be signed by [~accountid:60528926695c3900706cc79e] (or Ashmi’s equivalent manager).

Once the document has been signed, please ensure that it is uploaded to this ticket.

Separately, there needs to be a review of how the existing licence was allowed to expire and steps taken to ensure these circumstances are avoided in the future (i.e. ensuring contact details for licenses are kept up to date, a review process to check-up on circumstances where invoices are ‘missing’). That review can proceed outside of this ticket, but it is essential that this is properly addressed as losing premises associated with a ride-hailing licence is a key risk to our business. Our processes for the payment of invoices needs scrutinising, if this is also causing issues. However, we should not seek to address this by just telling our licensors to send invoices to our accounts team, as there does need to be some level of scrutiny by our operations team to ensure we are not paying improperly charged fees without anybody realising. 

Many thanks.

*Legal qualification*

There is no specific legal regulation of tipping in the Czech legal system. Therefore, general provisions apply to the legal regime of tips - according to the Czech legal system, tips can be qualified as a donation or a special reward according to the provisions of § 2060 of the Civil Code. Generally speaking, tipping is allowed as a donation. Therefore, in the sense of private law, the proposed model is acceptable.

 

*The entity to whom the tip is donated*

From the description of your proposed model, it is not clear to whom the tip belongs, or to which entity the tip is provided. Determining this entity is essential in order to determine which entity will receive the provided tip (or which entities will divide the tip among themselves and in what proportion). This entity designation also has tax implications (see below). The tip in your model can belong to: a) The restaurant preparing the food, b) Bolt as an intermediary, c) The courier as a self-employed entity (independent enterprenauer) or the employer of the person delivering the food, d) The courier as an employee, e) The tip is divided in different proportions between multiple entities.

So I recommend clarifying who the tip belongs to first.

 

*New T&C reflecting the new feature*

After clarifying who will receive the tip, it is appropriate to update your T&C of Bolt Food to reflect this new feature. The updated T&C should contain a transparent description of the new feature, an explanation of how it works, including a statement of which entity will receive a tip from the customer. If tipping will be conditional on customer satisfaction (by not contacting your customer support), then add this fact to the T&C as well.

 

*Tax implications*

For a proper assessment of the tax implications, it is necessary to distinguish who is the actual recipient of the tip (see previous paragraph). That is, if the tip is the income of an employee of the entrepreneur or if the tip is the income of the entrepreneur.

 

If the recipient of the tip is an employee, according to interpretative practice, it is income received in connection with the performance of a dependent activity and is subject to personal income tax according to the provisions of § 6 paragraph 1 letter d) of the Income Tax Act.

 

If the recipient is an entrepreneur, receiving a tip is considered as income from self-employment subject to corporate income tax according to the provisions of § 17 of the Income Tax Act.

 

Since the tip will be provided without cash, the tax is easily traceable for the financial administration. Therefore, +I recommend that you consult with your tax advisor about the way in which the tip will be taxed in order to avoid possible problems with taxation+.

The event sequence between block, unblock, and message is quite irregular. Need to find a way to correctly identify the first block event, next unblocking.

{noformat}with cleaned_log as 
(
	-- Clean out all messages as it is a noise for this use case
	select *
	from ext_delta_public.invoicing_cash_blocking_state_change_log
	where event_type <> 'message'
),
cashblocking_seq as 
(
	select 
		id, client_id, cash_unblock_balance_limit, max_negative_cash_blocking_balance, current_balance, currency, country_code,
		event_type, fee_calculator_id, "timestamp", 
		lead(event_type, 1) over(partition by client_id order by "timestamp") as next_event_type,
		lead("timestamp", 1) over(partition by client_id order by "timestamp") as next_timestamp,
		lag(event_type, 1) over(partition by client_id order by "timestamp") as prev_event_type,
		lag("timestamp", 1) over(partition by client_id order by "timestamp") as prev_timestamp,
		case when event_type <> coalesce(prev_event_type, 'first_event') then 1 else 0 end is_changing_event
	from cleaned_log
),
cashblocking_seq_partition as 
(
	select *, sum(is_changing_event) over(partition by client_id order by "timestamp" rows between unbounded preceding and current row) as event_partition
	from cashblocking_seq
),
remove_inbetween as 
(
	-- Remove event rows in between of first block and first unblock, chronologically
	select *
	from 
	(
		select *, row_number() over(partition by client_id, event_partition  order by "timestamp") as event_partition_seq
		from cashblocking_seq_partition 
	)
	where event_partition_seq = 1
),
true_event_attribute as 
(
	select *,
	lead(event_type, 1) over(partition by client_id order by "timestamp") as true_next_event_type,
	lead("timestamp", 1) over(partition by client_id order by "timestamp") as true_next_timestamp
	from remove_inbetween
)
select *,
	case when true_next_event_type = 'unblock' then 1 else 0 end as is_unblocked,
	case when true_next_event_type = 'unblock' then true_next_timestamp end as unblocked_time,
	datediff(minute, "timestamp", coalesce(unblocked_time, GETDATE())) as block_duration
from true_event_attribute 
where event_type = 'block'{noformat}
